Your pet probably had a wonderful loving and fun life with you and your family; your pet fulfilled its own purpose of being your friend and giving you affection. Sometimes life can seem like an empty barrel of suffering because it impacts so much every day; we see it on the news and we see it in our relatives and pets whom we love. My partner was sexually and physically abused as a child until he was 11 years old. This resulted in significant trauma and learning difficulties as he grew up, including violent outbursts; he was somewhat of a feral child for a time due to the severity of the abuse. He developed PTSD and already suffered from psychosis and bipolar disorder. He grew up in a low-income area, and his mother struggled with substance abuse. His trauma led him to deeply loathe himself.

He eventually turned to various substances due to family issues, poor coping mechanisms, trauma, and a lack of support. He also experienced homelessness for part of his life and ended up incarcerated for about a year.

He was a completely broken individual after his time in jail; when I look at pictures of him from the past, he appears entirely different from how he looks now.

It took him a while to get sober and escape his circumstances, but he endured an incredibly challenging life, and the abuse he suffered was horrific. He turned to drugs because he had no other options and was unaware of any alternatives. I can confidently say that incarceration did nothing to help him; it only broke him down further and hardened him. He did not deserve to go through that; he needed help, support, and proper care. The system failed him, and although he has been nearly two years clean, he did not deserve to be punished for his actions. The experiences he endured in jail and the things he was forced to do have led to ongoing suicidal thoughts, which he continues to struggle with alongside everything else.

My depression has been with me for a very long time and I did not know..looking back when I was younger it was quite obvious. I was withdrawn, had low interest/motivation, engaged in self-harm, etc. But my life was completely normal and happy. I have loving and supportive parents, so I'm not sure where it came from. It exacerbated when I had a lot of difficult situations happening in my life. A family member had a heart attack, I was cheated on, another family member lost their job, etc.

After all this turmoil stopped, I was bedridden for 2 weeks. Barely able to get up. All I did was sleep. I didn't even eat. It took me ages to get out of it. My negative thoughts permeated everything even though things in my life were improving so much (new job, healthy and loving relationship, more money, etc.). Even though things were going well, my brain made everything a struggle. Depression can cause confusion and memory issues. I still deal with some memory problems. Also, sometimes just physical pain from depression. It took me a while to realize I needed medication. But what I mean by rewiring your brain is stopping negative thoughts. Thoughts about worthlessness or things falling apart for no reason. I tell myself, "just because I think something doesn't mean it is true." Intrusive thoughts are so harmful at times, and just because you feel like things are going to fall apart doesn't mean they will.

Your brain is not you. All of this was a reaction to trauma. It messed up my body and way of thinking. You can believe whatever you'd like about society, and I'm not going to stop you. But what I mean is rewiring your brain so that you can live without negative intrusive thoughts. Negative thoughts can feel so real and true, but once again, all it is is just a thought and nothing more. Having a "whatever" attitude is hard to achieve, but life is short, and I'm not wasting time being negative. Instead, I'm going to enjoy hobbies and my own time.

My point is, even though things were going well, my brain was still in a state of war. I feel that depression can definitely be caused by having a difficult life for sure. But it can also be caused by genetics and trauma.

I'm not saying it's easier to recover from depression just because you haven't dealt with trauma. Depression is a tough battle. But I believe in you to overcome this. There is so much in this world.
